title: 2D Contour arc fit at a coarse tolerance sits 0.01 mm past the wall on a tessellated cylinder (verify holds it as a gouge), depending on walk direction

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while fixing #1555 (PR #1577).

**What happens.** `crates/ui/src/law_tests.rs::arc_moves_draw_curved` builds a 2D Contour around a Ø30 cylinder stock (`SrcRef::Stock`, Side Auto, EM-0400-2FL, tolerance 0.1). Walked clockwise (climb after #1555), `fit_arcs` fits three arcs about centre (-0.0034, 0.0034) with radius about 16.995, so the arcs dip about 0.010 mm inside the tool-radius offset. `verify` reports `Gouge` at every arc move (`[Gouge { at: 3 }, { at: 4 }, { at: 5 }, ...]`) and the post is held, so this is not silent. Walked counter-clockwise, the same ring fits two arcs plus two lines and passes, by luck of where the fitter splits. The fitter walks each ring from its own end, so the split points, and so the sag past the wall, depend on direction.

**Expected.** At any tolerance the user picks, the fitted contour does not cross the offset by more than the verify's gouge tolerance. Either the fit is one-sided (sag only into air) or the fitter re-splits an arc that dips past the offset. It should never produce a path the gate then refuses as a gouge.

**Workaround.** A finer tolerance (0.01) on the operation.

**Evidence.** On PR #1577's branch, set `climb: true` in `arc_moves_draw_curved` (that PR pins it on `climb: false` for now) and print `cache.warnings`.

Done means: a contour fitted at tolerance 0.1 on a tessellated round wall verifies clean in both walk directions, pinned by a test that runs both, and `arc_moves_draw_curved` goes back to the climb walk.
